  • AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.toPic_map

kleiman-picard For a morphism \(g \colon X \to Y\) of affine schemes, base change of Picard classes along the ring map \(g^{\# } \colon \Gamma (Y, \top ) \to \Gamma (X, \top )\) intertwines the Čech–Picard descent homomorphism (Definition 779) with the pullback of Čech classes; that is, for every \(L \in Y.\mathrm{CechPic}\),

\[ \mathrm{toPic}_X(g^{*} L) = \operatorname{Pic}(g^{\# })\bigl(\mathrm{toPic}_Y(L)\bigr) \quad \text{in } \operatorname{Pic}\bigl(\Gamma (X, \top )\bigr). \]

This is the separatedness half of Kleiman, The Picard Scheme, Theorem 2.5(1), in its Čech incarnation.

Proof ▶

Represent \(L\) by a unit cocycle \(\gamma \) on a pointed cover \(\mathcal U\) of \(Y\) and choose a finite basic refinement \(P\) of \(\mathcal U\). Then \(\mathrm{toPic}_Y(L)\) is the Picard class descended from the cover cocycle of \(\gamma \) on the finite localization cover \(P.r \colon P.\iota \to \Gamma (Y, \top )\). Base-changing this whole Čech picture along \(g^{\# }\) (Theorem 796) computes \(\operatorname{Pic}(g^{\# })(\mathrm{toPic}_Y L)\) as the Picard class of the pushed cover cocycle on the pushed family \(f'_i = g^{\# }(P.r_i)\), whose basic opens \(X.\mathrm{basicOpen}(f'_i) = g^{-1} Y.\mathrm{basicOpen}(P.r_i)\) are the pullbacks of \(P\)’s basic opens.

On the other side, \(\mathrm{toPic}_X(g^{*} L)\) is the Picard class descended from the cover cocycle of \(g^{*}\gamma \) on any finite basic refinement of the pulled-back cover \(\mathcal U^{\mathrm{pb}}\). As \(g\) need not be surjective, the pushed family \(f'\) is not itself a basic refinement of \(\mathcal U^{\mathrm{pb}}\); take the product refinement \(R\) indexed by \(P.\iota \times Q.\iota \), for an auxiliary basic refinement \(Q\) of \(\mathcal U^{\mathrm{pb}}\), with sections \(g^{\# }(P.r_i) \cdot Q.r_j\). The pushed cover cocycle, refined to \(R\) by the first projection, differs from the cover cocycle of \(g^{*}\gamma \) on \(R\) by the index-wise coboundary of the cross evaluations \(\gamma \) pulled back through \(g\); two point-selections on a common refinement always differ by such a coboundary. Since the descended Picard class is unchanged by a coboundary, the two Picard classes coincide, which is the asserted identity.

7.19 The class-level coherence seed for étale separatedness

Let \(k\) be a field and \(A \to B\) a homomorphism of \(k\)-algebras, and let \(C\) be a curve over \(k\). Write \(\operatorname{Spec}A, \operatorname{Spec}B\) for the corresponding test objects of \(\mathrm{Over}(\operatorname{Spec}k)\). This section records the class-level coherence seed of the (C1) étale-separatedness theorem — the separatedness half of Kleiman, The Picard Scheme, Theorem 2.5(1).

Definition 809 The two coprojections of a double cover of a test algebra
✓

The two coprojections of the double cover \(B \otimes _A B\) of \(B\) are the \(k\)-algebra homomorphisms

\[ \mathrm{tensorInl} \colon B \to B \otimes _A B, \quad b \mapsto b \otimes 1, \qquad \mathrm{tensorInr} \colon B \to B \otimes _A B, \quad b \mapsto 1 \otimes b. \]
Lemma 810 Diagonal coherence of the two coprojections
✓
#

Uses

  • Definition 809

Lean declarations

  • AlgebraicGeometry.tensorInl_comp_ofId

Precomposed with the base inclusion \(A \to B\), the two coprojections agree: \(\mathrm{tensorInl} \circ (A \to B) = \mathrm{tensorInr} \circ (A \to B)\) as \(k\)-algebra homomorphisms \(A \to B \otimes _A B\).

Proof ▶

For \(a \in A\) with image \(\bar a \in B\), both sides send \(a\) to \(\bar a \otimes 1\) respectively \(1 \otimes \bar a\); over \(A\) these are equal, \(\bar a \otimes 1 = a \cdot (1 \otimes 1) = 1 \otimes \bar a\), because tensoring is over \(A\).

Theorem 811 The class-level coherence seed
✓

Uses

kleiman-picard Let \(L\) be a Čech Picard class on the curve-product \(C \otimes \operatorname{Spec}A\) and \(N\) a Čech Picard class on \(\operatorname{Spec}B\). Suppose that over the test algebra \(A \to B\) the class \(L\) restricts to the pullback of \(N\) from the base:

\[ \mathrm{pr}_B^{*} N = (C \lhd \operatorname{Spec}(A \to B))^{*} L. \]

Then the two base changes of \(N\) to \(\operatorname{Spec}(B \otimes _A B)\) along the coprojections coincide: \(\operatorname{Spec}(\mathrm{tensorInl})^{*} N = \operatorname{Spec}(\mathrm{tensorInr})^{*} N\).

Proof ▶

For each coprojection \(j \in \{ \mathrm{tensorInl}, \mathrm{tensorInr}\} \), pull back \(\operatorname{Spec}(j)^{*} N\) along the projection \(\mathrm{pr}_{B \otimes _A B}\). Using functoriality of Čech pullback (Lemma 711), the base square of the projection (Lemma 800) and the hypothesis, this equals \((C \lhd \operatorname{Spec}(j \circ (A \to B)))^{*} L\). By the diagonal coherence (Lemma 810), \(\mathrm{tensorInl} \circ (A \to B) = \mathrm{tensorInr} \circ (A \to B)\), so the two composites \(\operatorname{Spec}(\mathrm{tensorInl})^{*} N\) and \(\operatorname{Spec}(\mathrm{tensorInr})^{*} N\) have the same pullback along \(\mathrm{pr}_{B \otimes _A B}\). Pullback along the curve projection is injective on Picard classes (Theorem 774), hence the two base changes agree.

7.20 The Amitsur toolkit for étale separatedness

This section collects three reusable groups of statements consumed by the coherent-witness step of the (C1) étale-separatedness assembly, all revolving around the fact that only global units cross the curve projection \(\mathrm{pr}\).

Let \(\mathcal U\) be a pointed cover of a scheme \(X\). A family of units \(\beta _x \in \Gamma (X, \mathcal U_x)^{\times }\) whose members agree on pairwise overlaps glues to a single global unit \(w \in \Gamma (X, \top )^{\times }\) restricting to each \(\beta _x\); and a global unit that restricts to \(1\) on every member of a pointed cover — more precisely, two global units agreeing on every member — is uniquely determined.

The members \(\mathcal U_x\) cover \(\top \) because \(x \in \mathcal U_x\). The gluing statement is the sheaf gluing for unit sections (Lemma 763) at the tautological cover \(V = \top \), \(W = \mathcal U\); the uniqueness statement is the separation for unit sections (Lemma 762) at the same cover.

Each identity is checked on a generator \(b \in B\): both sides insert \(b\) into the same tensor position and fill the remaining two positions with \(1\), by the definitions of the cofaces and coprojections.

7.21 The pullback calculus for unit cochains

The coherent-witness construction of the next section manipulates unit Čech cochains by pulling them back along morphisms of schemes and combining the results multiplicatively. This section records the elementary calculus of those operations over abstract schemes, so that the concrete instances in the construction are single applications.

Throughout, for a morphism \(f \colon X \to Y\), a unit section \(s \in \mathcal{O}_{Y}(V)^{\times }\) on an open \(V \subseteq Y\), and an open \(O \subseteq X\) contained in the preimage \(f^{-1}(V)\), write \(f^{\sharp }_O s \in \mathcal{O}_{X}(O)^{\times }\) for the pullback of \(s\) along \(f\), restricted to \(O\). This operation is a group homomorphism on units, is functorial in the morphism, \((r \circ f)^{\sharp }_O s = f^{\sharp }_O (r^{\sharp } s)\) whenever the composite is defined, and commutes with shrinking \(O\). When \(u \in \mathcal{O}_{Y}(\top )^{\times }\) is a global unit, its pullback \(f^{\sharp }_O(u|_\top )\) is the restriction to \(O\) of the global-section pullback \(f^{\sharp }_\top u \in \mathcal{O}_{X}(\top )^{\times }\).

Lemma 818 Congruence in the morphism
✓
#

Lean declarations

  • AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE_section_congr_hom
  • AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE_pair_congr_hom

Let \(g, g' \colon X \to Y\) be two morphisms with \(g = g'\), let \(V\) assign to each point of \(Y\) an open of \(Y\), and let \(s\) assign to each point \(y\) a unit section \(s_y \in \mathcal{O}_{Y}(V(y))^{\times }\). Then for every \(x \in X\) and every open \(O \subseteq g^{-1}(V(g(x)))\),

\[ g^{\sharp }_O\, s_{g(x)} = (g')^{\sharp }_O\, s_{g'(x)} . \]

The same holds for doubly point-indexed families \(V(y,y')\), \(s_{y,y'}\), such as the pair evaluations of a unit Čech cocycle.

Proof ▶

Since \(g = g'\), the two sides are identical: the equality of morphisms transports the source base point, the open \(V(g(x)) = V(g'(x))\), and the section \(s_{g(x)} = s_{g'(x)}\) simultaneously, so the pullbacks agree.

Lemma 819 Pullback of a coboundary relation
✓
#

Lean declarations

  • AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE_coboundary_rel

Let \(\varphi \colon X \to Y\), \(r_1 \colon Y \to Z_1\), \(r_2 \colon Y \to Z_2\). Suppose a unit \(0\)-cochain \(c\) on a pointed cover \(\mathcal C\) of \(Y\) cobounds the comparison of two pair-indexed unit families \(E_1\) on \(Z_1\) and \(E_2\) on \(Z_2\), pulled back along \(r_1\) and \(r_2\): for all \(y, y' \in Y\), on the overlap \(\mathcal C(y) \cap \mathcal C(y')\),

\[ c_y \cdot \bigl(r_1^{\sharp } E_1\bigr)_{y y'} = \bigl(r_2^{\sharp } E_2\bigr)_{y y'} \cdot c_{y'} . \]

Then for every \(x, x' \in X\) and every open \(O \subseteq \varphi ^{-1}(\mathcal C(\varphi x) \cap \mathcal C(\varphi x'))\), the pullback of the relation along \(\varphi \) holds in composite normal form:

\[ \varphi ^{\sharp }_O\, c_{\varphi x} \cdot \bigl((r_1\varphi )^{\sharp }_O E_1\bigr)_{x x'} = \bigl((r_2\varphi )^{\sharp }_O E_2\bigr)_{x x'} \cdot \varphi ^{\sharp }_O\, c_{\varphi x'}, \]

where \(r_i\varphi \) denotes the composite \(X \xrightarrow {\varphi } Y \xrightarrow {r_i} Z_i\).

Proof ▶

Apply the pullback homomorphism \(\varphi ^{\sharp }_O\) to both sides of the given relation at the points \(\varphi x, \varphi x'\). Being a group homomorphism on units it distributes over the products; and by functoriality it merges each pullback, \(\varphi ^{\sharp }_O(r_i^{\sharp } E_i) = (r_i\varphi )^{\sharp }_O E_i\), while leaving \(\varphi ^{\sharp }_O c\) unchanged. The two normal forms result.

Lemma 820 The global-unit pullback in restriction form
✓
#

Lean declarations

  • AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE_unitsRestrict_top
  • AlgebraicGeometry.unitsRestrict_top_self
  • AlgebraicGeometry.unitsAppLE_top_global

Let \(f \colon X \to Y\) and \(u \in \mathcal{O}_{Y}(\top )^{\times }\) a global unit. The restriction of \(u\) along \(\top \le \top \) is \(u\) itself; and for any point-indexed open \(V\) and any open \(O \subseteq f^{-1}(V)\), pulling the restricted unit back along \(f\) equals the restriction to \(O\) of the global-section pullback of \(u\):

\[ f^{\sharp }_O\bigl(u|_V\bigr) = \bigl(f^{\sharp }_\top u\bigr)\big|_O . \]

In particular, at \(V = \top \) the open-indexed and global spellings of pulling back a global unit coincide.

Proof ▶

The restriction along the identity inclusion \(\top \le \top \) is the identity map on sections. For the second identity, both sides are the image of \(u\) under one and the same ring map \(\mathcal{O}_{Y}(\top ) \to \mathcal{O}_{X}(O)\) — the composite of the comorphism of \(f\) on global sections with restriction to \(O\) — so they agree; the \(V = \top \) case is the same statement read backwards.

Lemma 821 Functoriality of the global-unit pullback
✓
#

Lean declarations

  • AlgebraicGeometry.units_map_appTop_comp

For morphisms \(f \colon X \to Y\), \(g \colon Y \to Z\) and a global unit \(u \in \mathcal{O}_{Z}(\top )^{\times }\), pulling \(u\) back along \(g\) and then along \(f\) equals pulling it back along the composite \(g \circ f\):

\[ f^{\sharp }_\top \bigl(g^{\sharp }_\top u\bigr) = (g \circ f)^{\sharp }_\top u . \]
Proof ▶

The comorphism of a composite of morphisms is the composite of the comorphisms in the reverse order; applying this on global sections and passing to units gives the claim.

✓

Lean declarations

  • AlgebraicGeometry.unitsAppLE_mulDiv_comp

Let \(\varphi \colon X \to Y\) and let \(a, b, c\) be pulled-back cochain values along morphisms \(g_1, g_2, g_3 \colon Y \to Z\), each a unit section on a common open \(V\) of \(Y\). For any open \(O \subseteq \varphi ^{-1}(V)\),

\[ \varphi ^{\sharp }_O\Bigl(\tfrac {a \cdot b}{c}\Bigr) = \frac{(g_1\varphi )^{\sharp }_O a \cdot (g_2\varphi )^{\sharp }_O b}{(g_3\varphi )^{\sharp }_O c}, \]

and likewise for a combination of the shape \(t \cdot (a/b)\); pushing the pullback through the combination merges each factor into a composite pullback.

7.22 The Amitsur-coherent Čech witness

Let \(k\) be a field, \(A \to B\) a homomorphism of \(k\)-algebras, and \(C\) an object of \(\mathrm{Over}(\operatorname{Spec}k)\) which is proper, geometrically irreducible and geometrically reduced over \(k\). Retain the coprojections \(q_1 = \operatorname{Spec}(\mathrm{tensorInl})\), \(q_2 = \operatorname{Spec}(\mathrm{tensorInr}) \colon \operatorname{Spec}B \to \operatorname{Spec}(B \otimes _A B)\) of Definition 809 and the three cofaces \(f_{12}, f_{13}, f_{23} = \operatorname{Spec}(\mathrm{tensorFace}_{\bullet }) \colon \operatorname{Spec}(B \otimes _A B) \to \operatorname{Spec}(B \otimes _A (B \otimes _A B))\) of Definition 813. This section implements the coherent-witness step of the étale-separatedness argument of Kleiman, The Picard Scheme: starting from the class equality \(q_1^{*} N = q_2^{*} N\) supplied by the class-level coherence seed (Theorem 811), it produces a Čech witness cochain that is moreover Amitsur-coherent over the triple tensor, correcting an arbitrary witness by a single global unit.

Uses

Take the cover of the witness to be \(\mathcal V\) and the cochain to be \(\theta = \theta _0/(\chi |)\), where \(\chi |\) is the restriction of the global unit \(\chi \) to the members of \(\mathcal V\). For the witness relation: dividing both sides of the witness relation for \(\theta _0\) by the central unit \(\chi \), which restricts the same way at \(x\) and \(y\), preserves it, so \(\theta \) is again a witness. For coherence: the Amitsur defect of \(\theta \) is the Amitsur defect of \(\theta _0\) divided by the Amitsur combination \((f_{23}^{\sharp }\chi )(f_{12}^{\sharp }\chi )/(f_{13}^{\sharp }\chi )\) of the coface restrictions of \(\chi \). Each coface pullback of the restricted global unit \(\chi \) is the restriction of its global-section pullback (Lemma 820), so this Amitsur combination is exactly the restriction of the global unit displayed in the hypothesis; by hypothesis it equals the Amitsur defect of \(\theta _0\). The quotient is therefore \(1\), i.e. \((f_{23}^{\sharp }\theta )(f_{12}^{\sharp }\theta ) = f_{13}^{\sharp }\theta \).

If \(\theta _0\) is a witness cochain for \(\gamma \) on a common refinement \(\mathcal V\) (satisfying the witness relation), then its Amitsur defect \(\partial \theta _0\) has trivial Čech coboundary and glues to a global unit \(\bar\omega \) on the triple tensor \(\operatorname{Spec}(B \otimes _A (B \otimes _A B))\), restricting to \(\partial \theta _0\) on each member of \(\mathcal V_{123}\).

Proof ▶

Pull the witness relation for \(\theta _0\) back along each of the three cofaces \(f_{23}, f_{12}, f_{13}\) (Lemma 819), obtaining on the Amitsur refinement three coboundary relations between the coface pullbacks of \(\theta _0\) and the pulled-back coprojections of \(\gamma \). By the coface coincidences (Lemma 824) the six composite maps \(f_{\bullet } \circ q_{\bullet }\) collapse onto the three insertions, so — after rewriting the point-indexed \(\gamma \)-terms accordingly (Lemma 818) — the three relations share matching \(\gamma \)-factors. Multiplying the \(f_{23}\)- and \(f_{12}\)-relations and dividing by the \(f_{13}\)-relation, the \(\gamma \)-factors cancel telescopically, leaving that the defect values \(\partial \theta _0\) at any two points of \(\mathcal V_{123}\) agree on their overlap. Thus \(\partial \theta _0\) is a compatible unit family, and by global gluing of a compatible family (Theorem 812) it glues to a global unit \(\bar\omega \).

Lemma 831 Compatibility of a ratio cochain from two coboundary relations
✓
#

Uses

  • Lemma 819
  • Lemma 818

Lean declarations

  • AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE_coboundary_ratio_compat

Let \(\varphi _t \colon X \to Y_c\) and \(\varphi _1, \varphi _2 \colon X \to Y_a\). Suppose a unit \(0\)-cochain \(c\) on \(Y_c\) cobounds the comparison of a family \(E_Z\) along two maps \(Y_c \to Z\), and a unit \(0\)-cochain \(a\) on \(Y_a\) cobounds the comparison of \(E_Z\) (along a map \(Y_a \to Z\)) with a family \(E_W\) (along a map \(Y_a \to W\)). If the pulled-back comparison composites coincide pairwise and the two maps \(\varphi _1, \varphi _2\) agree after the map to \(W\) (the diagonal coincidence), then the ratio cochain \(\varphi _t^{\sharp } c \cdot (\varphi _2^{\sharp } a / \varphi _1^{\sharp } a)\) on \(X\) is Čech-compatible: its values at any two points agree on a common open.

Proof ▶

Pull the two coboundary relations back to \(X\): the relation for \(c\) along \(\varphi _t\), and the relation for \(a\) along each of \(\varphi _1, \varphi _2\) (Lemma 819). The pairwise coincidence of composites lets us identify the \(E_Z\)-terms of the \(c\)-relation with those of the \(a\)-relations, and the diagonal coincidence identifies the two \(E_W\)-terms of the \(\varphi _1\)- and \(\varphi _2\)-pullbacks (Lemma 818). Writing \(Q_1, Q_2\) for the common \(E_Z\)-terms and \(L\) for the common \(E_W\)-term, the three relations read \(c_x Q_1 = Q_2 c_{x'}\), \(a_i Q_i = L\, a_i'\); a direct computation in the unit group then gives \(c_x (a_2/a_1) = c_{x'}(a_2'/a_1')\), which is compatibility of the ratio cochain.

Let \(\theta _0\) be a witness cochain for \(\gamma \) downstairs and \(\alpha \) a witness cochain upstairs for the lift — that is, \(\alpha \) cobounds the comparison of the projection pullback of \(\gamma \) with the pullback along \(C \lhd \operatorname{Spec}(A \to B)\) of a unit cocycle \(\lambda \) representing the class \(L\). Then the comparison cochain of \(\theta _0\) against \(\alpha \) is Čech-compatible, hence has trivial coboundary.

Proof ▶

Apply the compatibility principle for ratio cochains (Lemma 831) with \(\varphi _t = \mathrm{pr}\) and \(\varphi _1 = u_1\), \(\varphi _2 = u_2\): the witness relation for \(\theta _0\) downstairs and the witness relation for \(\alpha \) upstairs are the two coboundary relations. The base squares of the projection (Lemma 800) identify \(\mathrm{pr}\) followed by each coprojection \(q_i\) with \(u_i\) followed by the projection \(\mathrm{pr}_B\), giving the pairwise coincidence of the \(\gamma \)-composites; and the diagonal coincidence (Lemma 825) identifies \(u_1\) and \(u_2\) after the whiskered base inclusion, cancelling the \(\lambda \)-terms carrying the class \(L\). The hypotheses of Lemma 831 are met, and its conclusion is exactly compatibility of the comparison cochain.

Then the projection pullback of \(\chi \) is \(\psi \), which restricts to the comparison cochain on each member of the comparison cover.

Suppose the glued Amitsur defect \(\bar\omega \) of a witness cochain \(\theta _0\) restricts to the Amitsur defect \(\partial \theta _0\), and the comparison unit \(\chi \) pulls back on the curve product to the comparison cochain of \(\theta _0\) against an upstairs witness \(\alpha \). Then \(\bar\omega \) is the Amitsur coboundary of \(\chi \):

\[ \bar\omega = \frac{(f_{23}^{\sharp }\chi ) \cdot (f_{12}^{\sharp }\chi )}{f_{13}^{\sharp }\chi } . \]
Proof ▶

Both sides are global units on the triple tensor; since global-unit pullback along the curve projection is injective (Theorem 816), it suffices to compare their pullbacks to the triple-tensor curve product. Pull \(\bar\omega \) back along the projection: by Lemma 823 and the base squares of the projection (Lemma 800) it restricts to the Amitsur combination of the three whiskered-coface pullbacks of \(\theta _0\). Pull each coface pullback of \(\chi \) back along the projection: by functoriality of the global-unit pullback (Lemma 820, Lemma 821) and the base squares it becomes the corresponding whiskered-coface pullback of the descended comparison unit, which by Lemma 823 together with the coface coincidences (Lemma 824) restricts to the same \(\theta _0\)-term times a telescoping combination of correction factors built from \(\alpha \). Forming the Amitsur combination of the three, the \(\alpha \)-telescope cancels exactly, leaving precisely the Amitsur combination of \(\theta _0\)-terms found for \(\bar\omega \). The two global units thus have equal projection pullbacks, hence are equal.

kleiman-picard Let \(C\) be proper, geometrically irreducible and geometrically reduced over the field \(k\), let \(k \to A \to B\) be a tower of algebras, let \(L\) be a Čech Picard class on \(C \otimes \operatorname{Spec}A\), and let \(\gamma \) be a unit cocycle on a pointed cover \(\mathcal N\) of \(\operatorname{Spec}B\) whose class \(N\) pulls back, on the curve product, from \(L\): \(\mathrm{pr}_B^{*} N = (C \lhd \operatorname{Spec}(A \to B))^{*} L\). Then there exists an Amitsur-coherent Čech witness for \(\gamma \) — a witness for the class equality \(q_1^{*} N = q_2^{*} N\) over \(\operatorname{Spec}(B \otimes _A B)\) whose coface pullbacks are Amitsur-coherent over the triple tensor.

Proof ▶

By the class-level coherence seed (Theorem 811) the hypothesis gives the equality \(q_1^{*} N = q_2^{*} N\); unwinding it through the equality criterion for Čech Picard classes yields a common refinement \(\mathcal V\) of the two coprojection pullbacks of \(\mathcal N\) and a witness cochain \(\theta _0\) on it satisfying the witness relation. Likewise, the hypothesis \(\mathrm{pr}_B^{*} N = (C \lhd \operatorname{Spec}(A \to B))^{*} L\) yields an upstairs witness cochain \(\alpha \) on a cover \(\mathcal A\) of \(X_B\), cobounding the comparison of the projection pullback of \(\gamma \) with the pullback of a representative \(\lambda \) of \(L\). The Amitsur defect of \(\theta _0\) glues to a global unit \(\bar\omega \) (Theorem 830); the comparison of \(\theta _0\) against \(\alpha \) glues and descends to a global unit \(\chi \) on \(\operatorname{Spec}(B \otimes _A B)\) (Theorem 835); and \(\bar\omega \) is identified with the Amitsur coboundary of \(\chi \) (Theorem 836). Thus \(\chi \) satisfies the hypothesis of the correction lemma (Lemma 828), and the corrected cochain \(\theta _0/\chi \) is the required Amitsur-coherent Čech witness.

7.23 The simplicial degeneracies of the tensor tower

Complementing the cofaces of Definition 813 and their \(\operatorname{Spec}\)-level coincidences (Lemma 824), the composite descent unit pulls back along the two degeneracies of the tensor tower: the multiplication, whose \(\operatorname{Spec}\) is the diagonal, and the first-two-positions multiplication, whose \(\operatorname{Spec}\) is a degeneracy of the triple tensor.

Definition 838 The multiplication and the first degeneracy
✓

Lean declarations

  • AlgebraicGeometry.tensorMul
  • AlgebraicGeometry.descentMul₁₂
  • AlgebraicGeometry.tensorMul₁₂

The multiplication is the \(k\)-algebra homomorphism

\[ \mathrm{tensorMul} \colon B \otimes _A B \to B, \qquad x \otimes y \mapsto xy , \]

whose \(\operatorname{Spec}\) is the diagonal \(\Delta \colon \operatorname{Spec}B \to \operatorname{Spec}(B \otimes _A B)\). The first degeneracy is the \(k\)-algebra homomorphism multiplying the first two tensor positions,

\[ \mathrm{tensorMul}_{12} \colon B \otimes _A (B \otimes _A B) \to B \otimes _A B, \qquad x \otimes (y \otimes z) \mapsto xy \otimes z , \]

whose \(\operatorname{Spec}\) is the degeneracy \(\sigma \colon \operatorname{Spec}(B \otimes _A B) \to \operatorname{Spec}(B \otimes _A (B \otimes _A B))\).

Lemma 839 Degeneracy identities at ring level
✓

Uses

  • Definition 838

Lean declarations

The degeneracies satisfy the simplicial identities against the coprojections and cofaces:

\[ \mathrm{tensorMul} \circ \mathrm{tensorInl} = \mathrm{id}_B = \mathrm{tensorMul} \circ \mathrm{tensorInr} , \]

and, on the triple tensor,

\[ \mathrm{tensorMul}_{12} \circ \mathrm{tensorFace}_{23} = \mathrm{id}, \quad \mathrm{tensorMul}_{12} \circ \mathrm{tensorFace}_{13} = \mathrm{id}, \quad \mathrm{tensorMul}_{12} \circ \mathrm{tensorFace}_{12} = \mathrm{tensorInl} \circ \mathrm{tensorMul} . \]
Proof ▶

Each identity is an equality of \(k\)-algebra homomorphisms, checked on a generator. For the first pair, \(\mathrm{tensorMul}(\mathrm{tensorInl}\, b) = \mathrm{tensorMul}(b \otimes 1) = b\) and \(\mathrm{tensorMul}(\mathrm{tensorInr}\, b) = \mathrm{tensorMul}(1 \otimes b) = b\). For the degeneracy against the cofaces, compute on \(x \otimes y\): \(\mathrm{tensorMul}_{12}(1 \otimes (x \otimes y)) = x \otimes y\); \(\mathrm{tensorMul}_{12}(x \otimes (1 \otimes y)) = x \otimes y\); and \(\mathrm{tensorMul}_{12}(x \otimes (y \otimes 1)) = xy \otimes 1 = \mathrm{tensorInl}(xy) = \mathrm{tensorInl}(\mathrm{tensorMul}(x \otimes y))\).

7.24 The trivialization-corrected witness cochain

The values \(\theta _x\) of an Amitsur-coherent Čech witness (Definition 827) do not by themselves glue over a basic open of the tensor square: their coboundary is the comparison of the two coprojection pullbacks of \(\gamma \). The composite descent unit corrects them by cocycle values of \(\gamma \) anchored at two distinguished points, after which they glue, satisfy the Amitsur cocycle identity, and collapse onto the Zariski cover cocycle on the diagonal. This section develops that calculus over abstract schemes; the concrete tensor-tower instantiation is Section 7.25.

Throughout, \(r_1, r_2 \colon Y \to Z\) are two morphisms (playing the coprojections \(\operatorname{Spec}(B \otimes _A B) \to \operatorname{Spec}B\)); \(\mathcal C\) is a pointed cover of \(Y\) with a unit \(0\)-cochain \(c\) (the witness cover and cochain); \(\mathcal N\) is a pointed cover of \(Z\) with a unit cocycle \(\gamma _Z\) (the trivializing cover of \(\operatorname{Spec}B\)); \(a, b \in Z\) are two points; and \(D \subseteq Y\) is an open on which \(r_1\) lands in \(\mathcal N_a\) and \(r_2\) in \(\mathcal N_b\).

Definition 841 The corrected witness cochain
✓
#

Lean declarations

  • AlgebraicGeometry.unitsCorrCochain

The corrected witness value at a point \(y \in Y\) is the unit on \(\mathcal C_y \cap D\)

\[ (\mathrm{corr}\, c)_y := r_1^{\sharp }\gamma _Z(a,\, r_1 y) \cdot (c_y)^{-1} \cdot r_2^{\sharp }\gamma _Z(r_2 y,\, b) , \]

the two correction factors being the coprojection pullbacks of the cocycle values of \(\gamma _Z\) anchored \(a \to r_1 y\) on the left and \(r_2 y \to b\) on the right, with the witness entering inverted. This is the unique orientation whose coboundary cancels the coboundary of \(\theta ^{-1}\), and which on the diagonal — where the coherent witness is \(1\) — telescopes to the cocycle value \(\gamma _Z(a, b)\).

Assume the witness relation for \(c\): on the overlaps of \(\mathcal C\), \(c_x \cdot r_1^{\sharp }\gamma _Z(r_1 x, r_1 y) = r_2^{\sharp }\gamma _Z(r_2 x, r_2 y) \cdot c_y\). 7.26 Section rings on basic opens as two-base localizations

To pass the three identities of Section 7.25 to the pure-algebra assembly of Section 4.5, the section rings on the basic opens of the tensor towers are identified with the algebraic tensor localizations. All section rings of \(\operatorname{Spec}R\) carry the canonical \(R\)-algebra structure whose structure map is the inverse of the global-sections isomorphism \(\Gamma \operatorname{Spec}\)-iso followed by restriction.

The restriction maps of the section rings along the diagonal \(\Delta \) and the three cofaces correspond, under the identifications of Definition 856, to the index-wise collapse and faces of the pure-algebra assembly. Each is an instance of the uniqueness of maps out of a localization: both composites are computed on structure-map images and agree there, and extensionality is invoked over \(B \otimes _A B\) — where the components are \(\mathrm{Away}\) localizations — never over \(A\).

The global-sections isomorphism is an isomorphism of \(A\)-algebras \(\Gamma (\operatorname{Spec}B, \top ) \cong B\) for the composed \(A\)-structure. Consequently, if \(A \to B\) is faithfully flat, then \(A \to \Gamma (\operatorname{Spec}B, \top )\) is faithfully flat.

7.29 Faithfully flat descent of sections along the base change of the curve product

Fix a field \(k\), a curve \(C\) over \(k\) (proper, geometrically irreducible and geometrically reduced), and a tower \(k \to A \to B\) with \(A \to B\) faithfully flat. Write \(X_A := (C \otimes \operatorname{Spec}A)_{\mathrm{left}}\), \(X_B := (C \otimes \operatorname{Spec}B)_{\mathrm{left}}\), and \(\mathrm{cg} := (C \lhd \operatorname{Spec}(A \to B))_{\mathrm{left}} \colon X_B \to X_A\) for the base-change morphism of the curve product; the two coprojections \(u_1, u_2 \colon (C \otimes \operatorname{Spec}(B \otimes _A B))_{\mathrm{left}} \to X_B\) are the whiskered coprojections of \(B \otimes _A B\). This section proves that sections of the structure sheaf, and of its units, descend along \(\mathrm{cg}\): the fppf sheaf property along the whiskered base inclusion.

For an arbitrary open \(W\), if two sections have equal pullbacks, then their restrictions to each affine open \(V \subseteq W\) have equal pullbacks (pullback commutes with restriction), hence agree by the affine case; as the affine opens contained in \(W\) cover \(W\), the two sections agree by separation for the structure sheaf (Lemma 762).

Let \(U \subseteq X_A\) be an affine open. A unit \(t \in \Gamma (X_B, \mathrm{cg}^{-1}U)^{\times }\) whose two coprojection pullbacks agree, \(u_1^{*} t = u_2^{*} t\), descends to a unit: there is \(s \in \Gamma (X_A, U)^{\times }\) with \(\mathrm{cg}^{*} s = t\).

Proof ▶

Both \(t\) and \(t^{-1}\) satisfy the equalizer hypothesis, so by Theorem 868 they descend to sections \(a, b \in \Gamma (X_A, U)\) with \(\mathrm{cg}^{*} a = t\), \(\mathrm{cg}^{*} b = t^{-1}\). The pullback of \(ab\) is \(t t^{-1} = 1 = \mathrm{cg}^{*} 1\), so \(ab = 1\) by injectivity of the pullback over the affine open \(U\) (Theorem 869); likewise \(ba = 1\). Hence \(a\) is a unit and \(\mathrm{cg}^{*} a = t\).

7.30 Saturated affine pieces of the base-change cover

Retain the field \(k\), the curve \(C\) over \(k\), and the tower \(k \to A \to B\) of the previous section, with \(X_A = (C \otimes \operatorname{Spec}A)_{\mathrm{left}}\), \(X_B = (C \otimes \operatorname{Spec}B)_{\mathrm{left}}\), the projections \(\mathrm{pr}_A \colon X_A \to \operatorname{Spec}A\), \(\mathrm{pr}_B \colon X_B \to \operatorname{Spec}B\), and the base-change morphism \(\mathrm{cg} \colon X_B \to X_A\). This section refines the \(\top \)-case identification \(\Gamma (X_B, \top ) \cong B\) (Lemma 865) to an arbitrary affine open of \(X_A\): over such an open the section ring of the cover piece is the base change of the base section ring along \(A \to B\). Nothing here uses flatness or properness (except where explicitly assumed); these are the geometric pieces on which a covering-and-overlaps effectivity argument runs.

The base-change morphism \(\mathrm{cg} \colon X_B \to X_A\) is affine. Consequently the preimage \(\mathrm{cg}^{-1}U\) of every affine open \(U \subseteq X_A\) is affine.

Proof ▶

By the base-change square (Theorem 867, with \(T = \operatorname{Spec}A\), \(T' = \operatorname{Spec}B\) and \(g = \operatorname{Spec}(A \to B)\)) the morphism \(\mathrm{cg}\) is the base change of \(\operatorname{Spec}(A \to B) \colon \operatorname{Spec}B \to \operatorname{Spec}A\) along the projection \(\mathrm{pr}_A\). The morphism \(\operatorname{Spec}(A \to B)\) is affine, being the spectrum of a ring homomorphism, and affine morphisms are stable under base change; hence \(\mathrm{cg}\) is affine. \[ \begin{array}{ccc} A & \longrightarrow & \Gamma (X_A, U) \\ \downarrow & & \downarrow \mathrm{cg}^{\sharp } \\ B & \longrightarrow & \Gamma \bigl(X_B, \mathrm{cg}^{-1}U\bigr) \end{array} \]

Re-cornering along the canonical identifications \(\Gamma (\operatorname{Spec}A, \top ) \cong A\) and \(\Gamma (\operatorname{Spec}B, \top ) \cong B\) (which intertwine the structure maps, as in Lemma 865) replaces those two corners by \(A\) and \(B\), yielding the displayed pushout.

Let \(\mathrm{lam}\) be a unit Čech cocycle on a pointed cover \(\mathcal E\) of \(X_A\), and let \(\beta \) be a unit \(0\)-cochain on a pointed cover \(\mathcal A\) of \(X_B\) refining the base-change pullback of \(\mathcal E\), trivializing the pulled-back cocycle: on overlaps, \(\beta _v \cdot (\mathrm{cg}^{\sharp }\mathrm{lam})_{vv'} = \beta _{v'}\). Then there is a global unit \(w \in \Gamma (\operatorname{Spec}(B \otimes _A B), \top )^{\times }\) such that

  1. on the common refinement of the two coprojection pullbacks of \(\mathcal A\), the curve-product pullback of \(w\) is the ratio \(u_1^{*}\beta / u_2^{*}\beta \) of the two coprojection pullbacks of \(\beta \); and

  2. the \(\Gamma \operatorname{Spec}\)-avatar of \(w\) in \((B \otimes _A B)^{\times }\) is a descent \(1\)-cocycle relative to \(A \to B\).

Proof ▶

The two coprojection pullbacks \(u_1^{*}\beta , u_2^{*}\beta \) are units over the members of the common refinement \(u_1^{*}\mathcal A \cap u_2^{*}\mathcal A\), and their ratio is compatible on overlaps: the coboundary hypothesis on \(\beta \), pulled back through the coprojection compatibility \(u_1 \circ \mathrm{cg} = u_2 \circ \mathrm{cg}\) of the whiskered faces, cancels the two \(\mathrm{lam}\)-factors and leaves the ratios agreeing on double overlaps. By gluing of unit sections (Theorem 812) the ratio family glues to a global section, which by surjectivity of the global-section pullback (Theorem 816) is the curve-product pullback of a global unit \(w\) on \(\operatorname{Spec}(B \otimes _A B)\); this is (1).

For (2), work upstream on \(\operatorname{Spec}(B \otimes _A (B \otimes _A B))\). Applying the three Amitsur cofaces (Definition 813) to the local ratio form of \(w\) and using the simplicial coincidences among the coprojections, the \(\beta \)-telescope cancels exactly to give the cocycle identity \((f_{23}^{\sharp } w)(f_{12}^{\sharp } w) = f_{13}^{\sharp } w\) of the avatar. The diagonal normalization \(\mu (w) = 1\) is the whiskered degeneracy of the tensor diagonal (Definition 838, Lemma 839, Lemma 840), under which the two coprojection pullbacks of \(\beta \) coincide and their ratio is \(1\). These are exactly the descent \(1\)-cocycle conditions (Definition 783) for the avatar of \(w\).

7.32 The Čech representative of a descended Picard class

The descent unit \(w\) of the previous section is the descent datum of an invertible module \(\mathrm{descended}(w)\) over \(A\). This section presents the Čech class of that module on \(\operatorname{Spec}A\), together with the trivializing units of its base change to \(\operatorname{Spec}B\), whose coprojection ratio is exactly \(w\). Throughout, \(\mathrm{gS} := \operatorname{Spec}(A \to B)_{\mathrm{left}} \colon \operatorname{Spec}B \to \operatorname{Spec}A\) and \(q_1, q_2 \colon \operatorname{Spec}(B \otimes _A B) \to \operatorname{Spec}B\) are the two coprojections.

\[ \mathrm{evalT} \colon \Gamma (\operatorname{Spec}A, V) \otimes _A N \longrightarrow \Gamma (\operatorname{Spec}B, U), \qquad s \otimes m \longmapsto (\mathrm{gS}^{*} s) \cdot \bigl(\Gamma \operatorname{Spec}^{-1} m\bigr) \big|_{U}, \]

Let \(w \in \Gamma (\operatorname{Spec}(B \otimes _A B), \top )^{\times }\) and suppose every \(m \in N\) satisfies the descent equation of \(w\): \(1 \otimes m = \Gamma \operatorname{Spec}(w) \cdot (m \otimes 1)\) in \(B \otimes _A B\). Then, over any open \(O\) below both coprojection preimages of \(U\), the two coprojection pullbacks of an evaluation differ by the restriction of \(w\):

\[ q_2^{*}\bigl(\mathrm{evalT}(x)\bigr) = w|_{O} \cdot q_1^{*}\bigl(\mathrm{evalT}(x)\bigr), \qquad x \in \Gamma (\operatorname{Spec}A, V) \otimes _A N. \]
Proof ▶

The two coprojections send the section factor \(\mathrm{gS}^{*} s\) to the same value, the pullback along the common composite \(q_1 \circ \mathrm{gS} = q_2 \circ \mathrm{gS}\); and they send the module factor to the two coprojection-avatars \(\Gamma \operatorname{Spec}^{-1}(m \otimes 1)\) and \(\Gamma \operatorname{Spec}^{-1}(1 \otimes m)\) (Definition 809). The descent equation of \(w\) applied to \(m\) turns the second avatar into \(w\) times the first, and the central unit \(w\) factors out, giving the stated ratio.

7.34 The Čech kernel lemma and the close of étale separatedness

The pieces now compose. The kernel lemma isolates the genuinely fppf content — a Čech class killed by the cover pullback is pulled back from the base — and the class-level reduction and the plus unfold deliver, from it, the injectivity of the unit of the étale plus construction: Kleiman’s separatedness of the relative Picard functor.

Theorem 886 The Čech kernel lemma
✓

Uses

kleiman-picard Let \(C\) be proper, geometrically irreducible and geometrically reduced over \(k\), and \(A \to B\) faithfully flat. Then the kernel of the base-change pullback \(\mathrm{cg}^{*} \colon \operatorname{Pic}(X_A) \to \operatorname{Pic}(X_B)\) is contained in the image of the projection pullback \(\mathrm{pr}_A^{*} \colon \operatorname{Pic}(\operatorname{Spec}A) \to \operatorname{Pic}(X_A)\): every class \(E\) on \(X_A\) with \(\mathrm{cg}^{*} E = 1\) is \(\mathrm{pr}_A^{*} M_1\) for some class \(M_1\) on \(\operatorname{Spec}A\).

Proof ▶

Represent \(E\) by a unit cocycle \(\mathrm{lam}\) on a pointed cover \(\mathcal E\) of \(X_A\). Since \(\mathrm{cg}^{*} E = 1\), the pulled-back cocycle is a coboundary: there is a trivializing \(0\)-cochain \(\beta \) on a refinement of \(\mathrm{cg}^{*}\mathcal E\) with \(\beta _v \cdot (\mathrm{cg}^{\sharp }\mathrm{lam})_{vv'} = \beta _{v'}\). Feed \((\mathcal E, \mathrm{lam}, \beta )\) to the descent unit (Theorem 880), obtaining a global unit \(w\) whose avatar is a descent \(1\)-cocycle; take a Čech representative \((\mathcal C, d, \mu )\) of its descended class (Theorem 884). Refine \(\mathcal E \cap \mathrm{pr}_A^{-1}\mathcal C\) to a cover \(\mathcal U\) by affine opens (Lemma 769); on each chart \(U = \mathcal U(s)\), the cobounding unit (Theorem 885) gives \(c_s \in \Gamma (X_A, U)^{\times }\).

It remains to check that the \(c_s\) cobound \(\mathrm{lam}\), restricted to \(\mathcal U\), against the \(\mathrm{pr}_A\)-pullback of the representing cocycle \(d\); that is,

\[ c_s|_{U_s \cap U_t} \cdot \mathrm{pr}_A^{*} d_{\, \mathrm{pr}_A s,\, \mathrm{pr}_A t} = \mathrm{lam}_{s t}\big|_{U_s \cap U_t} \cdot c_t|_{U_s \cap U_t}. \]

Both sides pull back injectively along \(\mathrm{cg}\) (Theorem 869); after pullback, the glued local forms of \(c_s, c_t\), the \(\mu \)-transition of the representative, and the cocycle identity of \(\mathrm{lam}\) telescope to the required identity. Hence \(\mathrm{lam}\) and \(\mathrm{pr}_A^{*} d\) are cohomologous on \(\mathcal U\), so \([\mathcal U, \mathrm{lam}] = \mathrm{pr}_A^{*}[\mathcal C, d]\) by refinement injectivity in degree one (Theorem 765, Corollary 766); that is, \(E = \mathrm{pr}_A^{*} M_1\) with \(M_1 = [\mathcal C, d]\). This is the descent-datum step of Kleiman’s separatedness argument in its Čech incarnation: the trivialization \(\beta \) descends the class from the faithfully flat cover to the base.

From the hypothesis \(\mathrm{pr}_B^{*} N_0 = \mathrm{cg}^{*} L\), the coherent Čech witness (Theorem 837) provides an Amitsur-coherent trivialization of the two coprojection pullbacks of \(N_0\), and the assembly of the previous chapter builds from it a composite \(A\)-descent unit whose avatar is a descent \(1\)-cocycle (Theorem 863). Let \(M\) be the Čech class on \(\operatorname{Spec}A\) corresponding, through the Čech–Picard dictionary (Theorem 782), to the Picard class of the descended module (Definition 785) of that composite unit. By the class equation of the assembly (Theorem 866) and naturality of the dictionary in the affine scheme (Theorem 807), the base change \(\mathrm{gS}^{*} M\) has the same descent homomorphism image as \(N_0\); since that homomorphism is injective (Theorem 780), \(\mathrm{gS}^{*} M = N_0\) on the nose. Then, using the projection base square (Lemma 800),

\[ \mathrm{cg}^{*}\bigl(\mathrm{pr}_A^{*} M\bigr) = \mathrm{pr}_B^{*}\bigl(\mathrm{gS}^{*} M\bigr) = \mathrm{pr}_B^{*} N_0 = \mathrm{cg}^{*} L , \]

so \(L \cdot (\mathrm{pr}_A^{*} M)^{-1}\) is killed by \(\mathrm{cg}^{*}\). The kernel property yields \(M_1\) with \(\mathrm{pr}_A^{*} M_1 = L \cdot (\mathrm{pr}_A^{*} M)^{-1}\), whence \(L = \mathrm{pr}_A^{*}(M \cdot M_1)\).

Fix \(A\). Suppose the kernel property of the base-change pullback holds for every tower \(A \to B\) with \(A \to B\) faithfully flat. Then the unit \(\eta _A \colon \mathrm{relPic}(C,A) \to \mathrm{PicEtAff}(C,A)\) of the plus construction (Definition 740) is injective.

Proof ▶

As \(\eta _A\) is a group homomorphism it suffices to show its kernel is trivial. Let \(x = [\operatorname{Spec}A, L] \in \mathrm{relPic}(C,A)\) with \(\eta _A(x) = 1\). Unwinding the plus-class equality \([\mathrm{self}(A), \iota ^{*}x] = 1\) through the presentation criterion (Theorem 730) and the essential uniqueness of \(A\)-algebra maps out of \(A\), the datum reduces to a single presented étale cover \(A \to B_G\): the base change \((\mathrm{ofId}\ A\ B_G)^{*}L\) lies in the descent-trivial subgroup of \(\mathrm{relPic}(C,B_G)\) (Definition 712, Definition 719). Concretely there is a class \(N_0\) on \(\operatorname{Spec}B_G\) with \(\mathrm{pr}_{B_G}^{*} N_0 = \mathrm{cg}^{*} L\) — the hypothesis of the reduction. Since a presented étale cover is in particular faithfully flat, the reduction (Theorem 887) pulls \(L\) back from the base, \(L = \mathrm{pr}_A^{*} M\); that is exactly \(x = 1\) in \(\mathrm{relPic}(C,A)\), using the normalization of the unit at the identity (Definition 735).

kleiman-picard Let \(C\) be a curve over \(k\) that is proper, geometrically irreducible and geometrically reduced, and let \(A\) be any \(k\)-algebra. Then the unit \(\eta _A \colon \mathrm{relPic}(C,A) \to \mathrm{PicEtAff}(C,A)\) of the one-step étale plus construction is injective. Equivalently, the relative Picard functor of \(C\) is separated for the étale topology — the separatedness half of Kleiman, The Picard Scheme, Theorem 2.5(1).

The kernel property of the base-change pullback holds for every faithfully flat tower \(A \to B\) by the Čech kernel lemma (Theorem 886). Feeding it to the plus unfold (Theorem 888) gives the injectivity of \(\eta _A\). This is exactly Part 1 of Kleiman’s comparison theorem in the étale case: the natural map \(\operatorname{Pic}_{X/S} \hookrightarrow \operatorname{Pic}_{(X/S)\mathrm{\acute et}}\) is injective, so a single étale plus computes the sheafification and \(\mathrm{PicEtAff}\) is separated on the étale site of affines.

7.35 Unit sections across an open immersion

Throughout this section \(w \colon Z \to Y\) is an open immersion of schemes. Over an open \(V \subseteq Y\) contained in the image of \(w\), pullback of sections along \(w\) is bijective; this transports unit sections between \(Y\) and \(Z\) and is the substrate for decomposing Čech Picard classes along clopen partitions.

Lemma 890 Units over an empty open form a trivial group
✓
#

Lean declarations

  • AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.subsingleton_units_of_le_bot

For a scheme \(X\) and an open \(O \subseteq X\) with \(O \subseteq \emptyset \) (that is, \(O = \emptyset \)), the unit group \(\Gamma (X, O)^{\times }\) is trivial (a subsingleton).

Proof ▶

Since \(O = \emptyset \), the ring \(\Gamma (X, O)\) is the zero ring, in which \(0 = 1\) is the only element; hence its group of units has a single element.

Lemma 891 Sections pull back isomorphically over an open inside the image
✓
#

Lean declarations

  • AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isIso_appLE_of_le_opensRange

Let \(V \subseteq Y\) be an open with \(V \subseteq \operatorname {range}(w)\). Then pullback of sections along \(w\) is an isomorphism of rings \(\Gamma (Y, V) \xrightarrow {\ \sim \ } \Gamma (Z, w^{-1}V)\).

Proof ▶

An open immersion \(w\) identifies \(Z\) with the open subscheme \(\operatorname {range}(w)\) of \(Y\); for an open \(V\) contained in that image the comparison map on sections is the restriction isomorphism of the structure sheaf between \(V\) and its homeomorphic preimage \(w^{-1}V\). Hence pullback of sections over \(V\) is an isomorphism of rings.

For an open \(V \subseteq Y\) with \(V \subseteq \operatorname {range}(w)\), the isomorphism of unit groups

\[ \Gamma (Y, V)^{\times } \xrightarrow {\ \sim \ } \Gamma (Z, w^{-1}V)^{\times } \]

induced by pullback of sections along \(w\).

Proof ▶

Pullback of sections along \(w\) is an isomorphism of rings over \(V\) (Lemma 891); an isomorphism of rings restricts to an isomorphism of their groups of units.

7.36 Decomposition of the Čech Picard group along a clopen partition

A clopen partition of a scheme \(Y\) is a family of open immersions \(w_i \colon Z_i \to Y\), \(i \in \iota \), whose ranges are pairwise disjoint (\(\operatorname {range}(w_i) \cap \operatorname {range}(w_j) = \emptyset \) for \(i \ne j\)) and cover \(Y\); each range is then open with open complement. This section proves that the Čech Picard group of \(Y\) decomposes along such a partition: separation along an arbitrary clopen partition, and gluing along a finite one. Throughout, \(\operatorname{Pic}(Y)\) is the definitional Čech Picard group recalled in Section 7.19, with pullback \(w^{*} \colon \operatorname{Pic}(Y) \to \operatorname{Pic}(Z)\) along a morphism \(w \colon Z \to Y\).

Theorem 893 Separation of Čech Picard classes along a clopen partition
✓
#

Uses

  • Definition 892
  • Lemma 890
  • Corollary 767
  • Lemma 762
  • Lemma 763

Lean declarations

  • AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.eq_of_map_eq_of_clopen

Let \((w_i)_{i \in \iota }\) be a clopen partition of \(Y\). Two Čech Picard classes \(L, L' \in \operatorname{Pic}(Y)\) with \(w_i^{*} L = w_i^{*} L'\) for every \(i\) are equal.

Proof ▶

Choose for each point \(y \in Y\) an index \(p(y)\) with \(y \in \operatorname {range}(w_{p(y)})\). Represent \(L = [\mathcal U_1, a_1]\) and \(L' = [\mathcal U_2, a_2]\) and pass to the common adapted pointed cover \(\mathcal V(y) := \mathcal U_1(y) \cap \mathcal U_2(y) \cap \operatorname {range}(w_{p(y)})\), so that \(\mathcal V(y) \subseteq \operatorname {range}(w_{p(y)})\) for every \(y\); it suffices to show the ratio cocycle \(\gamma \) representing \(L/L'\) on \(\mathcal V\) is a coboundary.

Triviality on each piece. Fix \(i\). Since \(w_i^{*}L = w_i^{*}L'\), the pullback classes \(w_i^{*}[\mathcal V, a_1|_{\mathcal V}]\) and \(w_i^{*}[\mathcal V, a_2|_{\mathcal V}]\) are represented on the pulled-back pointed cover \(\mathcal V^{(i)} := w_i^{-1}\mathcal V\) by the pulled-back cocycles, and they agree in \(\operatorname{Pic}(Z_i)\); by refinement injectivity (Corollary 767) already the pulled-back ratio cocycle \(w_i^{\sharp }\gamma \) is a coboundary on \(\mathcal V^{(i)}\): there are units \(\alpha ^{(i)}_z \in \mathcal{O}_{Z_i}(\mathcal V^{(i)}(z))^{\times }\) with \(\alpha ^{(i)}_z \cdot (w_i^{\sharp }\gamma )_{zz'} = \alpha ^{(i)}_{z'}\) on the overlaps.

Gluing the piece coboundaries. For each \(y \in Y\), let \(z_0\) be the unique point of \(Z_{p(y)}\) over \(y\) (an open immersion is injective on points), and set \(\beta _y := \Phi ^{-1}\bigl(\alpha ^{(p(y))}_{z_0}|_{w_{p(y)}^{-1}\mathcal V(y)}\bigr) \in \Gamma (Y, \mathcal V(y))^{\times }\), where \(\Phi \) is the unit transport of Definition 892 across \(w_{p(y)}\) (applicable since \(\mathcal V(y) \subseteq \operatorname {range}(w_{p(y)})\)). The choice of index is forced: if \(y \in \operatorname {range}(w_i)\) too, then \(y \in \operatorname {range}(w_i) \cap \operatorname {range}(w_{p(y)})\), which is empty unless \(i = p(y)\); and the choice of preimage point is forced by injectivity.

\(\beta \) cobounds \(\gamma \). Fix \(y, y'\). If \(p(y') = p(y)\), both members lie in the single piece \(Z_{p(y)}\); the coboundary relation for \(\alpha ^{(p(y))}\) pulls back injectively through \(w_{p(y)}\) on the overlap \(\mathcal V(y) \cap \mathcal V(y') \subseteq \operatorname {range}(w_{p(y)})\) (pullback of unit sections is injective on opens inside the range, Definition 892), yielding \(\beta _y \cdot \gamma _{yy'} = \beta _{y'}\) there. If \(p(y') \ne p(y)\), then \(\mathcal V(y) \cap \mathcal V(y') \subseteq \operatorname {range}(w_{p(y)}) \cap \operatorname {range}(w_{p(y')}) = \emptyset \), so the units over the overlap form a trivial group (Lemma 890) and the relation holds vacuously. Assembling over the cover of \(\mathcal V(y) \cap \mathcal V(y')\) by these two cases and separating (Lemma 762; gluing across pieces uses Lemma 763 in the construction of \(\beta \)), \(\gamma = \delta \beta \) is a coboundary, so \(L/L' = 1\), i.e. \(L = L'\).

Theorem 894 The one-piece extension across a clopen decomposition
✓
#

Uses

  • Definition 892
  • Lemma 890

Lean declarations

  • AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.extendClass
  • AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.map_extendClass
  • AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.map_extendClass_of_le_compl

Let \(w \colon Z \to Y\) be an open immersion whose range is complemented by an open \(\Omega ' \subseteq Y\): \(\operatorname {range}(w) \cap \Omega ' = \emptyset \) and \(\operatorname {range}(w) \cup \Omega ' = Y\). For every \(L_0 \in \operatorname{Pic}(Z)\) there is a class \(\widetilde L \in \operatorname{Pic}(Y)\) with

\[ w^{*}\widetilde L = L_0, \qquad v^{*}\widetilde L = 1 \text{ for every } v \colon W \to Y \text{ with image contained in } \Omega '. \]
Proof ▶

Represent \(L_0 = [\mathcal U_0, \gamma _0]\) by a unit cocycle on a pointed cover of \(Z\). Build the extension cover \(\mathcal E\) of \(Y\): at a point \(y \in \operatorname {range}(w)\) take the \(w\)-image of the member of \(\mathcal U_0\) at the unique preimage of \(y\); at \(y \notin \operatorname {range}(w)\) take \(\Omega '\) (a legitimate pointed cover, since \(\operatorname {range}(w) \cup \Omega ' = Y\)). Define its pair values: on range–range overlaps the transported cocycle value \(\Phi ^{-1}\bigl((\gamma _0)_{\cdot \cdot }\bigr)\) of Definition 892 across \(w\), and \(1\) whenever either argument lies off the range. These satisfy the cocycle identity: on triple overlaps of range members it is the transported cocycle identity of \(\gamma _0\); every other triple overlap meets a range member and a non-range member, hence lies in \(\operatorname {range}(w) \cap \Omega ' = \emptyset \) and carries only the trivial unit (Lemma 890), so the identity degenerates. This produces \(\widetilde L := [\mathcal E, \text{extension cocycle}] \in \operatorname{Pic}(Y)\).

Restriction on the piece. The given cover \(\mathcal U_0\) refines the pullback \(w^{-1}\mathcal E\) (the preimage of the image of a member is that member), and along this refinement the pulled-back extension cocycle restricts to \(\gamma _0\) (its range–range values are the transported \(\gamma _0\)). Hence \(w^{*}\widetilde L = [\mathcal U_0, \gamma _0] = L_0\).

Restriction off the piece. For \(v \colon W \to Y\) with image in \(\Omega '\), every point \(v(x)\) lies off \(\operatorname {range}(w)\) (else it would lie in \(\operatorname {range}(w) \cap \Omega ' = \emptyset \)); so every pulled-back pair value is \(1\), the pulled-back cocycle is trivial, and \(v^{*}\widetilde L = 1\).

Theorem 895 Gluing of Čech Picard classes along a finite clopen partition
✓
#

Uses

  • Theorem 894

Lean declarations

  • AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.exists_map_eq_of_clopen

Let \((w_i)_{i \in \iota }\) be a finite clopen partition of \(Y\). Every family \((L_i)_{i \in \iota }\) with \(L_i \in \operatorname{Pic}(Z_i)\) is the family of restrictions of a single class \(M \in \operatorname{Pic}(Y)\): \(w_i^{*} M = L_i\) for all \(i\).

Proof ▶

For each \(i\), set \(\Omega '_i := \bigcup _{j \ne i} \operatorname {range}(w_j)\). By pairwise disjointness \(\operatorname {range}(w_i) \cap \Omega '_i = \emptyset \), and since the ranges cover \(Y\), \(\operatorname {range}(w_i) \cup \Omega '_i = Y\). Let \(M_i \in \operatorname{Pic}(Y)\) be the one-piece extension of \(L_i\) across \((w_i, \Omega '_i)\) (Theorem 894). Put \(M := \prod _{i} M_i\) (finite product). For each \(i\), pullback along \(w_i\) is a homomorphism, so \(w_i^{*} M = \prod _j w_i^{*} M_j\). The factor \(j = i\) is \(w_i^{*} M_i = L_i\); every factor \(j \ne i\) is \(1\), because \(\operatorname {range}(w_i) \subseteq \Omega '_j\) means \(w_i\) has image in the complement of the \(j\)-th piece, so \(w_i^{*}M_j = 1\) (Theorem 894). Hence \(w_i^{*} M = L_i\).

7.37 The relative Picard group of a finite product of test algebras

Fix a field \(k\) and a curve \(C\) over \(k\). For a finite family \((B_i)_{i \in \iota }\) of commutative \(k\)-algebras with product \(P := \prod _i B_i\), the spectrum of \(P\) is the disjoint union of the spectra of the factors, clopen-partitioned by the basic opens of the coordinate idempotents; base-changing along the curve, the whiskered coordinate projections clopen-partition the curve-product. Through the clopen decomposition of the previous section this identifies the relative Picard group of the product test with the product of the relative Picard groups of the factors. Write \(e_i \in P\) for the coordinate idempotent (\(1\) in slot \(i\), \(0\) elsewhere) and \(\pi _i \colon P \to B_i\) for the projection.

Lemma 896 Range of a whiskered open immersion
✓
#

Uses

  • Theorem 867

Lean declarations

  • AlgebraicGeometry.Over.range_whiskerLeft

Let \(g \colon T' \to T\) be a morphism of test objects with \(g_{\mathrm{left}}\) an open immersion. Then the whiskered morphism \((C \lhd g)_{\mathrm{left}}\) is an open immersion, and its range is the preimage under the second projection \(\mathrm{pr} \colon (C \otimes T)_{\mathrm{left}} \to T_{\mathrm{left}}\) of the range of \(g_{\mathrm{left}}\):

\[ \operatorname {range}\bigl((C \lhd g)_{\mathrm{left}}\bigr) = \mathrm{pr}^{-1}\bigl( \operatorname {range}(g_{\mathrm{left}})\bigr). \]
Proof ▶

The whiskering square with horizontal legs \((C \lhd g)_{\mathrm{left}}\), \(g_{\mathrm{left}}\) and vertical legs the two second projections is a pullback of schemes (Theorem 867). Open immersions are stable under base change, so \((C \lhd g)_{\mathrm{left}}\), being the base change of \(g_{\mathrm{left}}\) along \(\mathrm{pr}\), is an open immersion; and the range of the base change of an open immersion along \(\mathrm{pr}\) is the \(\mathrm{pr}\)-preimage of its range.

Lemma 897 A factor is the localization away from the coordinate idempotent
✓
#

Lean declarations

  • AlgebraicGeometry.isLocalization_away_piFactor

For a finite product \(P = \prod _j B_j\) and an index \(i\), the projection \(\pi _i \colon P \to B_i\) exhibits \(B_i\) as the localization of \(P\) away from the coordinate idempotent \(e_i\).

Proof ▶

The element \(e_i\) is idempotent, \(e_i^2 = e_i\). Two elements \(x, y \in P\) have the same image in \(B_i\) iff they agree in slot \(i\), iff \(e_i x = e_i y\) (multiplication by \(e_i\) zeroes every other slot). And every \(b \in B_i\) is the image of \(\mathrm{single}_i(b) \in P\). By the criterion for a localization away from an idempotent, \(B_i = P[e_i^{-1}]\).

Lemma 898 The coordinate projections clopen-partition the spectrum of a product
✓
#

Uses

  • Lemma 897
  • Definition 710

Lean declarations

  • AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_overSpecMap_evalAlgHom
  • AlgebraicGeometry.opensRange_overSpecMap_evalAlgHom_disjoint
  • AlgebraicGeometry.exists_mem_opensRange_overSpecMap_evalAlgHom

The morphisms \(\operatorname{Spec}\pi _i \colon \operatorname{Spec}B_i \to \operatorname{Spec}P\) (for the finite family \((B_i)_{i \in \iota }\)) are open immersions with pairwise disjoint ranges covering \(\operatorname{Spec}P\): the range of \(\operatorname{Spec}\pi _i\) is the basic open \(D(e_i)\), and \(D(e_i) \cap D(e_j) = \emptyset \) for \(i \ne j\) while \(\bigcup _i D(e_i) = \operatorname{Spec}P\).

Proof ▶

By Lemma 897, \(\pi _i\) realizes \(B_i\) as a localization of \(P\) away from \(e_i\), so \(\operatorname{Spec}\pi _i\) is an open immersion with range the basic open \(D(e_i)\) (the spectrum of a localization away from an element is that element’s basic open). For \(i \ne j\), \(e_i e_j = 0\), whence \(D(e_i) \cap D(e_j) = D(e_i e_j) = D(0) = \emptyset \). Finally \(\sum _i e_i = 1\); since \(\iota \) is finite, no prime of \(P\) contains all the \(e_i\) (it would then contain \(1\)), so every prime lies in some \(D(e_i)\), i.e. the ranges cover.

For a finite family \((B_i)_{i \in \iota }\) with product \(P\), two relative Picard classes \(\zeta , \zeta ' \in \mathrm{relPic}(C, P)\) with \(\pi _i^{*}\zeta = \pi _i^{*}\zeta '\) in \(\mathrm{relPic}(C, B_i)\) for every \(i\) are equal.

It remains to show \(\mathrm{pr}^{*} M = L/L'\) on the curve-product; then \(\zeta = \zeta '\). By separation along this partition (Theorem 893) it suffices to check equal pullback along each whiskered projection. \[ (C \lhd \operatorname{Spec}\pi _i)_{\mathrm{left}}^{*}(\mathrm{pr}^{*} M) = \mathrm{pr}^{*}\bigl(\operatorname{Spec}\pi _i^{*} M\bigr) = \mathrm{pr}^{*} N_i = (C \lhd \operatorname{Spec}\pi _i)_{\mathrm{left}}^{*}(L/L'), \]

as required.

7.38 Zariski separation of the étale plus construction

Throughout, \(k\) is a field and \(C\) is a curve over \(k\) (proper, geometrically irreducible, geometrically reduced). This section proves that the affine étale plus \(\mathrm{PicEtAff}(C, -)\) is a separated presheaf for the Zariski topology of affine tests: two plus classes over \(A\) agreeing on a finite covering family of localizations agree. The argument is instance-free of étale separatedness; it consumes only the product decomposition of the relative Picard group.

Let \(A\) be a \(k\)-algebra and \((g_i)_{i \in \iota }\) a finite family with \(\sum _i (g_i) = (1)\), and let \(S_i\) be the localization of \(A\) away from \(g_i\). Given presented étale covers \(K_i\) of \(S_i\), the product \(\prod _i B_{K_i}\) is the carrier of a presented étale cover \(W\) of \(A\), with an isomorphism of \(A\)-algebras \(B_W \cong \prod _i B_{K_i}\).

Proof ▶

Each \(S_i\), a localization of \(A\) away from \(g_i\), is étale over \(A\); each \(B_{K_i}\) is étale over \(S_i\), hence over \(A\); so the finite product \(\prod _i B_{K_i}\) is étale over \(A\). It remains that \(\operatorname{Spec}(\prod _i B_{K_i}) \to \operatorname{Spec}A\) is surjective; then \(\prod _i B_{K_i}\) is a presented étale cover of \(A\) (Definition 690, Lemma 691). Given a prime \(p\) of \(A\): since \(\sum _i (g_i) = (1)\), some \(g_i \notin p\), so \(p\) lifts to \(\operatorname{Spec}S_i\) (the spectrum of the localization away from \(g_i\) is the basic open \(D(g_i) \ni p\)); as \(K_i\) is a cover of \(S_i\) it is surjective on spectra (Definition 689), so \(p\) lifts further to \(\operatorname{Spec}B_{K_i}\), and thence to \(\operatorname{Spec}(\prod _j B_{K_j})\) through the \(i\)-th coordinate. Hence the structure map is surjective.

Let \(A\) be a \(k\)-algebra, \((g_i)_{i \in \iota }\) a finite family with \(\sum _i (g_i) = (1)\), and \(S_i\) the localization of \(A\) away from \(g_i\). Two plus classes \(x, y \in \mathrm{PicEtAff}(C, A)\) with equal restrictions along every \(A \to S_i\) are equal.

Proof ▶

Restriction is a homomorphism, so it suffices to show a class \(z\) with trivial restriction to every \(S_i\) is trivial. Represent \(z = [G, \zeta ]\) (Lemma 729). For each \(i\), comparing the restriction of \([G, \zeta ]\) with that of the trivial class \([\mathrm{self}(A), 1]\) over \(S_i\) and unfolding (Theorem 901), there are a presented étale cover \(K_i\) of \(S_i\) and a homomorphism \(m_i \colon B_G \to B_{K_i}\), semilinear over \(A \to S_i\), with \(m_i^{*}\zeta = 1\) in \(\mathrm{relPic}(C, B_{K_i})\). Assemble the product cover \(W\) of \(A\) from the \(K_i\) (Theorem 902), \(B_W \cong \prod _i B_{K_i}\) over \(A\). The joint map \(\langle m_i \rangle \colon B_G \to \prod _i B_{K_i}\) pushes \(\zeta \) to a class whose \(i\)-th factor is \(\pi _i^{*}(\langle m_i\rangle ^{*}\zeta ) = m_i^{*}\zeta = 1\); by the product separation (Theorem 899) the pushed class is trivial in \(\mathrm{relPic}(C, \prod _i B_{K_i})\), hence in \(\mathrm{relPic}(C, B_W)\) after transport through the carrier isomorphism. As the joint map is an \(A\)-algebra refinement \(B_G \to B_W\), \([G, \zeta ] = [W, 1] = 1\) (Theorem 736). So \(z = 1\).

For a presented étale cover \(E\) of \(R\) and \(z \in \mathrm{relPic}(C, R)\), the unit \(\eta _R(z)\) is represented on \(E\) by the tautological descent datum of \(z\):

\[ \eta _R(z) = [E, \iota _E^{*}z], \qquad \iota _E^{*}z \in \mathrm{Desc}(C, E), \]

where \(\iota _E \colon R \to B_E\) is the structure map.

Proof ▶

By Lemma 731, transporting a representative along a refinement map does not change the plus class, so \([E, \iota _E^{*}z] = [E, \mathrm{fromSelf}_{*}(\iota ^{*}z)] = [\mathrm{self}(R), \iota ^{*}z] = \eta _R(z)\).

For a presented étale cover \(E\) of \(R\), restriction of relative Picard classes along the structure map \(\iota _E \colon R \to B_E\) is injective: if \(x, y \in \mathrm{relPic}(C, R)\) satisfy \(\iota _E^{*}x = \iota _E^{*}y\) in \(\mathrm{relPic}(C, B_E)\), then \(x = y\). This is what licenses every gluing step of the Layer-2 functor.

Proof ▶

By the étale separatedness of the relative Picard functor (Theorem 889), the unit \(\eta _R\) is injective, so it suffices to show \(\eta _R(x) = \eta _R(y)\). Represent both on \(E\) (Theorem 904): \(\eta _R(x) = [E, \iota _E^{*}x]\) and \(\eta _R(y) = [E, \iota _E^{*}y]\). Since \(\iota _E^{*}x = \iota _E^{*}y\) by hypothesis, these classes coincide, so \(\eta _R(x) = \eta _R(y)\) and hence \(x = y\).

Theorem 906 The pair condition
✓

Uses

  • Theorem 905
  • Theorem 901
  • Theorem 724

Lean declarations

  • AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.relPicAlgMap_tensor_eq_of_compat

Let \(S_1, S_2\) be localizations of a \(k\)-algebra \(A\) away from \(g_1, g_2\), and \(T_v\) a localization away from \(g_1 g_2\), with \(A\)-algebra homomorphisms \(\varphi _1 \colon S_1 \to T_v\), \(\varphi _2 \colon S_2 \to T_v\). Let \(E_1\) be a presented étale cover of \(S_1\), \(E_2\) of \(S_2\), and \(\xi _1 \in \mathrm{Desc}(C, E_1)\), \(\xi _2 \in \mathrm{Desc}(C, E_2)\). If \(\varphi _1^{*}[E_1, \xi _1] = \varphi _2^{*}[E_2, \xi _2]\) in \(\mathrm{PicEtAff}(C, T_v)\), then the two pullbacks of the underlying classes into the \(A\)-tensor product agree:

\[ \mathrm{inl}^{*}\xi _1 = \mathrm{inr}^{*}\xi _2 \quad \text{in } \mathrm{relPic}(C, B_{E_1} \otimes _A B_{E_2}), \]

where \(\mathrm{inl} \colon B_{E_1} \to B_{E_1} \otimes _A B_{E_2}\) and \(\mathrm{inr} \colon B_{E_2} \to B_{E_1} \otimes _A B_{E_2}\) are the two coprojections.

Proof ▶

Unfold the overlap compatibility (Theorem 901): there are a presented étale cover \(H\) of \(T_v\) and homomorphisms \(m_1 \colon B_{E_1} \to B_H\), \(m_2 \colon B_{E_2} \to B_H\), semilinear over \(\varphi _1, \varphi _2\), with \(m_1^{*}\xi _1 = m_2^{*}\xi _2\) in \(\mathrm{relPic}(C, B_H)\).

In \(B_{E_1} \otimes _A B_{E_2}\), the element \(g_1 g_2\) is a unit: \(g_1\) is a unit in \(B_{E_1}\) and \(g_2\) in \(B_{E_2}\) (both localized-away), and their images multiply to \(g_1 g_2\). Since \(T_v\) is the localization of \(A\) away from \(g_1 g_2\), there is a unique homomorphism of \(A\)-algebras \(\rho \colon T_v \to B_{E_1} \otimes _A B_{E_2}\). Base-change \(H\) along \(\rho \) to a presented étale cover \(W := H_{B_{E_1} \otimes _A B_{E_2}}\) (Definition 703), with canonical inclusion \(\theta \colon B_H \to B_W\). By the (C1) consumable (Theorem 905), restriction along the structure map \(B_{E_1} \otimes _A B_{E_2} \to B_W\) is injective; it therefore suffices to show that the two sides become equal after transport into \(B_W\).

Consider the two routes \(B_{E_1} \to B_W\). The first is \(\mathrm{inl}\) followed by the structure map into \(B_W\); the second is \(\theta \circ m_1\). Both are homomorphisms of \(S_1\)-algebras: for the second, \(m_1\) is \(\varphi _1\)-semilinear and \(\rho \circ \varphi _1\) equals the \(S_1\)-structure map \(S_1 \to B_{E_1} \otimes _A B_{E_2}\) (two homomorphisms of \(A\)-algebras out of the localization \(S_1\), hence equal). By refinement independence (Theorem 724, applied to the two \(S_1\)-algebra maps out of the cover \(E_1\) of \(S_1\) and the descent class \(\xi _1\)), the two routes transport \(\xi _1\) to the same class in \(\mathrm{relPic}(C, B_W)\). Symmetrically the two routes \(B_{E_2} \to B_W\) (namely \(\mathrm{inr}\) into \(B_W\) and \(\theta \circ m_2\)) transport \(\xi _2\) equally. Now

\[ (\theta \circ m_1)^{*}\xi _1 = \theta ^{*}(m_1^{*}\xi _1) = \theta ^{*}(m_2^{*}\xi _2) = (\theta \circ m_2)^{*}\xi _2 , \]

so, chaining the two refinement independences, the transports into \(B_W\) of \(\mathrm{inl}^{*}\xi _1\) and \(\mathrm{inr}^{*}\xi _2\) agree; by injectivity, \(\mathrm{inl}^{*}\xi _1 = \mathrm{inr}^{*}\xi _2\).

Lemma 907 Restriction along an algebra isomorphism is injective
✓

Uses

Lean declarations

  • AlgebraicGeometry.relPicAlgMap_algEquiv_injective

For an isomorphism of \(k\)-algebras \(e \colon A \xrightarrow {\ \sim \ } B\), restriction of relative Picard classes along \(e\), \(e^{*} \colon \mathrm{relPic}(C, A) \to \mathrm{relPic}(C, B)\), is injective.

Proof ▶

Restriction along \(e^{-1}\) is a left inverse: \((e^{-1})^{*} \circ e^{*} = (e^{-1} \circ e)^{*} = (\operatorname{id}_A)^{*} = \operatorname{id}\), by functoriality (Lemma 713). A map with a left inverse is injective.

Let \(\varphi \colon A_1 \to R\) be a homomorphism of \(k\)-algebras, \(E_1\) a presented étale cover of \(A_1\), \(F\) a presented étale cover of \(R\), \(\xi \in \mathrm{Desc}(C, E_1)\) and \(\eta \in \mathrm{Desc}(C, F)\). Suppose there is a homomorphism of \(k\)-algebras \(n \colon B_{E_1} \to B_F\), semilinear over \(\varphi \) (\(n \circ \iota _{E_1} = \iota _F \circ \varphi \)), with \(n^{*}\xi = \eta \) in \(\mathrm{relPic}(C, B_F)\). Then \(\varphi ^{*}[E_1, \xi ] = [F, \eta ]\).

Proof ▶

Regard \(R\) as an \(A_1\)-algebra through \(\varphi \), so that \(\varphi ^{*}[E_1, \xi ] = [(E_1)_R, \kappa _{E_1}^{*}\xi ]\) (Definition 744, with \((E_1)_R\) the base change, Definition 703). The semilinear map \(n\) extends uniquely to an \(R\)-algebra refinement \(n_R \colon B_{(E_1)_R} \to B_F\) with \(n_R \circ \kappa _{E_1} = n\). By the presentation criterion (Theorem 730, with the common cover \(F\), the map \(n_R\) out of \((E_1)_R\) and the identity out of \(F\)), \([(E_1)_R, \kappa _{E_1}^{*}\xi ] = [F, (n_R)_{*}(\kappa _{E_1}^{*}\xi )]\); and \((n_R)_{*}(\kappa _{E_1}^{*}\xi ) = n^{*}\xi = \eta \) by functoriality (Definition 712). Hence \(\varphi ^{*}[E_1, \xi ] = [F, \eta ]\).

Let \(A\) be a \(k\)-algebra, \((g_i)_{i \in \iota }\) a finite family with \(\sum _i (g_i) = (1)\), \(S_i\) the localization of \(A\) away from \(g_i\), and \(T_{ij}\) the localization away from \(g_i g_j\). A family \((x_i)_{i \in \iota }\) with \(x_i \in \mathrm{PicEtAff}(C, S_i)\), compatible on the overlaps (the restrictions of \(x_i\) and \(x_j\) to \(T_{ij}\) agree for all \(i, j\)), is the family of restrictions of a plus class \(z \in \mathrm{PicEtAff}(C, A)\): restriction of \(z\) to \(S_i\) is \(x_i\). Together with Theorem 903 this is the Zariski sheaf property of \(\mathrm{PicEtAff}(C, -)\) on affine tests.

Proof ▶

Represent \(x_i = [E_i, \xi _i]\) (Lemma 729). For each \(i, j\), the overlap compatibility over \(T_{ij}\) yields, by the pair condition (Theorem 906), \(\mathrm{inl}^{*}\xi _i = \mathrm{inr}^{*}\xi _j\) in \(\mathrm{relPic}(C, B_{E_i} \otimes _A B_{E_j})\). Lift the underlying classes to the product: by the product gluing (Theorem 900) there is \(\zeta \in \mathrm{relPic}(C, \prod _i B_{E_i})\) with \(\pi _i^{*}\zeta = \xi _i\). Assemble the product cover \(W\) of \(A\) from the \(E_i\) (Theorem 902), \(B_W \cong \prod _i B_{E_i}\) over \(A\); transport \(\zeta \) to \(\zeta _W \in \mathrm{relPic}(C, B_W)\).

\(\zeta _W\) is a descent class on \(W\). The descent condition \(\mathrm{inl}^{*}\zeta _W = \mathrm{inr}^{*}\zeta _W\) in \(\mathrm{relPic}(C, B_W \otimes _A B_W)\) is checked through the \(\pi \)-decomposition of the tensor square, \(B_W \otimes _A B_W \cong \prod _{(i, j)} B_{E_i} \otimes _A B_{E_j}\): by injectivity of transport along this isomorphism (Lemma 907) and product separation over the index set \(\iota \times \iota \) (Theorem 899), it suffices to compare components. The \((i, j)\)-component of \(\mathrm{inl}^{*}\zeta _W\) is \(\mathrm{inl}^{*} (\pi _i^{*}\zeta ) = \mathrm{inl}^{*}\xi _i\) and of \(\mathrm{inr}^{*}\zeta _W\) is \(\mathrm{inr}^{*}(\pi _j^{*}\zeta ) = \mathrm{inr}^{*}\xi _j\); these agree by the pair conditions.

The glued class. Set \(z := [W, \zeta _W]\). Its restriction to \(S_i\) is \(x_i\): the \(i\)-th projection \(B_W \cong \prod _j B_{E_j} \to B_{E_i}\) is a homomorphism semilinear over \(A \to S_i\) carrying \(\zeta _W\) onto \(\pi _i^{*}\zeta = \xi _i\), so by Lemma 908, \((A \to S_i)^{*}[W, \zeta _W] = [E_i, \xi _i] = x_i\).

7.41 The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor: the affine-opens limit

The frozen group-object interface forces the relative Picard functor to exist on all of \(\mathrm{Over}(\operatorname{Spec}k)\), not only on affine tests. Following the resolution of the Layer-2 vehicle question, the extension is the bespoke affine-opens limit: a section over a test object \(T\) is a compatible family of affine-level plus classes over the affine opens of \(T_{\mathrm{left}}\). The index poset is \(\mathrm{Type}\)-small, which is the point of the vehicle. Throughout, \(k\) is a field and \(C\) is a curve over \(k\).

kleiman-picard For a test object \(T\) of \(\mathrm{Over}(\operatorname{Spec}k)\), \(\mathrm{picEt}(C, T)\) is the group of compatible families: an element assigns to each affine open \(V \subseteq T_{\mathrm{left}}\) a plus class \(s_V \in \mathrm{PicEtAff}(C, \Gamma (T, V))\) such that for affine opens \(U \subseteq V\), the value \(s_U\) is the restriction of \(s_V\) along the section-restriction homomorphism \(\Gamma (T, V) \to \Gamma (T, U)\) (Definition 744). Componentwise product makes \(\mathrm{picEt}(C, T)\) a commutative group, a subgroup of the product \(\prod _{V} \mathrm{PicEtAff}(C, \Gamma (T, V))\); evaluation at an affine open \(V\) is the homomorphism \(s \mapsto s_V\). On affine tests this is the plus itself (the affine comparison, Definition 913); on general tests it is the canonical Zariski-continuous extension — the realization on all test objects of the étale sheafification \(\operatorname{Pic}_{(X/S)\mathrm{\acute et}}\) of the relative Picard functor.

Proof ▶

The compatibility condition is closed under the componentwise group operations: the constant family \(1\) is compatible (restriction preserves the identity); and if \(s, t\) are compatible, so are \(s \cdot t\) and \(s^{-1}\), because restriction of plus classes is a homomorphism of groups (Definition 744). Hence the compatible families form a subgroup of the product group, which is therefore a commutative group.

Definition 913 The affine comparison isomorphism
✓

Uses

  • Definition 910

Lean declarations

  • AlgebraicGeometry.picEtAffineEquiv

On an affine test \(\operatorname{Spec}A\), evaluation at the top affine open \(\top \) is a group isomorphism

\[ \mathrm{picEt}(C, \operatorname{Spec}A) \xrightarrow {\ \sim \ } \mathrm{PicEtAff}(C, A), \]

transported through the identification \(\Gamma (\top ) \cong A\) of Definition 911.

Proof ▶

The affine-opens poset of \(\operatorname{Spec}A\) has a terminal element, the top open \(\top \) (all of \(\operatorname{Spec}A\), an affine open containing every affine open), so a compatible family is determined by its value at \(\top \). The forward map sends \(s\) to \(s_\top \) carried through \(\Gamma (\top ) \cong A\) (Definition 911, Definition 910). The backward map sends \(x \in \mathrm{PicEtAff}(C, A)\) to the family whose value at \(V\) is \(x\) carried to \(\Gamma (\top )\) and restricted to \(\Gamma (V)\) (Definition 744); this family is compatible because restriction is functorial (restricting from \(\top \) to \(V\) and then to \(U\) is restricting to \(U\)). The two are mutually inverse: forward-then-backward recovers a family \(s\) from its \(\top \)-value, since \(s_V\) is the restriction of \(s_\top \) by the compatibility of \(s\) at \(V \subseteq \top \); backward-then-forward returns \(x\), since restriction from \(\top \) to \(\top \) is the identity and \(\Gamma (\top ) \cong A\) cancels. Both maps are homomorphisms of groups, so this is a group isomorphism.

7.42 Functoriality by the unique-pullback-value characterization

The Layer-2 functor \(\mathrm{picEt}\) is functorial along an arbitrary morphism \(f \colon T' \to T\) of test objects. The value of the restricted family at an affine open \(W \subseteq T'_{\mathrm{left}}\) — whose \(f\)-image need not lie in any affine open of \(T_{\mathrm{left}}\) — is glued over a finite basic-open refinement of \(W\) subordinate to the preimages of affine opens, using the Zariski sheaf property of the affine étale Picard functor. Throughout, \(C\) is a curve over \(k\).

Let \(W\) be an affine open of a scheme \(X\) and \(P\) a property of opens such that every point of \(W\) has an open neighbourhood inside \(W\) satisfying \(P\). Then there is a finite family of sections \(r \in \Gamma (X, W)\) spanning the unit ideal whose basic opens \(D(r)\) each lie inside some open satisfying \(P\).

Proof ▶

For each \(w \in W\), choose an open \(U_0 \ni w\) with \(P(U_0)\); since the basic opens of the affine \(W\) form a basis of its topology, choose \(r_w \in \Gamma (X, W)\) with \(w \in D(r_w) \subseteq U_0\). The \(D(r_w)\) cover \(W\); as \(W\) is quasi-compact (being affine), finitely many \(D(r_{w_1}), \dots , D(r_{w_n})\) already cover \(W\), which means the \(r_{w_j}\) span the unit ideal of \(\Gamma (X, W)\). Each \(D(r_{w_j}) \subseteq U_0\) lies inside an open with \(P\).

Refine \(W_0\) by basic opens: for each point \(w \in W_0\), the image \(f(w) \in V \cap V'\) lies in an affine open \(V'' \subseteq V \cap V'\) of \(T_{\mathrm{left}}\); choose a basic open \(D(r) \ni w\) of \(W_0\) with \(f(D(r)) \subseteq V''\), i.e. \(D(r) \subseteq f^{-1}V''\). By Theorem 914 a finite family of such \(r\) spans the unit ideal. On each \(D(r)\), the pullback of \(s_V\) restricted to \(\Gamma (T', D(r))\) factors as the pullback of \(s_{V''}\): using the compatibility \(s_{V''} = s_V|_{V''}\) (as \(V'' \subseteq V\)) and the functoriality of section pullback and restriction, it equals the pullback of \(s_{V''}\) along \(f\) from \(V''\) to \(D(r)\); likewise for \(s_{V'}\). Hence the two pullbacks agree on every \(D(r)\), so by Theorem 915 they agree on \(\Gamma (T', W_0)\).

For fixed \((f, s, W)\), a plus class with the pullback-value property is unique: if \(v, v'\) both have the property, then \(v = v'\).

Proof ▶

Refine \(W\) by basic opens \(D(r)\) each contained in the preimage of an affine open of \(T_{\mathrm{left}}\): every point of \(W\) maps into some affine open \(V\) of \(T_{\mathrm{left}}\), so has a basic-open neighbourhood in \(W\) inside \(f^{-1}V\; \)by Theorem 914 a finite such family spans the unit ideal. On each \(D(r) \subseteq f^{-1}V\), both \(v\) and \(v'\) restrict to the pullback of \(s_V\) (the defining property, Definition 916), hence agree. By Theorem 915, \(v = v'\).

Theorem 919 Existence of the pullback value

Uses

Lean declarations

For every \(f \colon T' \to T\), \(s \in \mathrm{picEt}(C, T)\) and affine open \(W\) of \(T'_{\mathrm{left}}\), there exists a unique plus class \(v \in \mathrm{PicEtAff}(C, \Gamma (T', W))\) with the pullback-value property for \((f, s, W)\).

Proof ▶

Choose (Theorem 914) a finite family \((r)\) in \(\Gamma (T', W)\) spanning the unit ideal such that each \(D(r)\) lies in the preimage \(f^{-1}V_r\) of an affine open \(V_r\) of \(T_{\mathrm{left}}\) (every point of \(W\) maps into some affine open). On \(D(r)\) take the local value to be the pullback of \(s_{V_r}\) along \(f\). On an overlap \(D(r) \cap D(r') = D(r r')\), the two local values agree: both restrict, through the affine opens \(V_r, V_{r'}\), to the same plus class by choice independence (Theorem 917). The section rings \(\Gamma (T', D(r))\) are localizations of \(\Gamma (T', W)\) away from the \(r\), which span the unit ideal, and the overlaps are localizations away from \(r r'\); so by the Zariski gluing of the plus construction (Theorem 909) the local values glue to a plus class \(v \in \mathrm{PicEtAff}(C, \Gamma (T', W))\).

This \(v\) has the pullback-value property: for an affine \(W_0 \subseteq W\) inside \(f^{-1}V\), refine \(W_0\) by basic opens \(D(q)\) each inside some \(D(r)\) (Theorem 914). On \(D(q)\), \(v\) restricts through the glued datum on \(D(r)\) to the pullback of \(s_{V_r}\), which by choice independence (Theorem 917) equals the pullback of \(s_V\); by Theorem 915, the restriction of \(v\) to \(\Gamma (T', W_0)\) equals the pullback of \(s_V\). Uniqueness is Theorem 918.

Definition 920 Restriction of \(\mathrm{picEt}\) along an arbitrary morphism
